name: migration
description: Workflow for moving a system, API, or schema from one shape to another: understand the current state, migration plan, execute, verify, review, and ship only when the rollback path is real.

stages.purpose: Establish what the current implementation actually does before planning the move.
Own the migration strategy, the compatibility window, and the rollback path.
Pin the behaviour that must survive the move with tests written before the change.
Review the migration for leftover compatibility shims and silent behaviour drift.
Prepare the rollout and rollback only when the migration is actually going out.

rules: Complete each stage before treating it as complete.
The stage order is the shape of the work, not permission to migrate first and test later: cover the behaviour that must survive the move with tests before changing the code that provides it.
Never drop an old code path until the new one has proven itself in production-side conditions.
Keep the compatibility window explicit and time-boxed; an open-ended shim is a decision, not a default.
Do not claim verification that did not happen.
Record every irreversible step before taking it.
completion: The migration is complete when the new path is verified, the old path is either removed or explicitly deprecated with a date, and the rollback path has been rehearsed.
